items.statement: For every g and every w ∈ ^MW: the complexes M_w^• ⊗ Q_p of Λ ⊗ Q_p-modules have amplitude [ℓ(w), g(g+1)/2], and the complexes M^•_{w,cusp} ⊗ Q_p have amplitude [0, ℓ(w)].
items.note: Corollary 6.2.17, p. 64; Theorem 1.4.3(3), p. 5. The proof is one line: 'This follows from 6.2.15 combined with [BP21], thm. 6.7.3'. Over the local rings of Λ ⊗ Q_p, vanishing of cohomology above degree b bounds the top of a minimal complex, but vanishing below degree a does not bound its bottom. The bottom bound comes from the top bound for the Serre-dual complex (Theorem 1.4.8, pairing M_w^• with M^•_{w_{0,M}ww_0,cusp}), combined with the other range in [BP21] Theorem 6.7.3. The one-line proof leaves this implicit. It is the rational form, over the whole weight space, of Pilloni (2020), Theorem 1.1. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Remark 6.2.18 (Conjecture 5.6.1 holds after inverting p)
items.statement: For every g and every w ∈ ^MW, RΓ_w(K^p) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p and RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p satisfy the vanishing of Conjecture 5.6.1, with amplitudes [ℓ(w), g(g+1)/2] and [0, ℓ(w)] respectively. That is, Conjecture 5.6.1 holds rationally.
items.note: Remark 6.2.18, p. 64: 'Dually we deduce the analogous vanishing results for RΓ_w(K^p) ⊗ Q_p and RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) ⊗ Q_p', through Lemma 5.4.2. Definition 1.4.1 defines amplitude for admissible complexes integrally only, so its meaning after inverting p is not defined. The natural reading is cohomological: H^i(RΓ_w(K^p) ⊗ Q_p) = 0 for i ∉ [ℓ(w), g(g+1)/2], and H^i(RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) ⊗ Q_p) = 0 for i ∉ [0, ℓ(w)]. Planned nowhere. The introduction states this result as Theorem 1.4.3(3) (p. 5), labelled 'Rational cohomological vanishing 6.2.17'. Corollary 6.2.17 (p. 64) is the corresponding statement for M^•_w ⊗ Q_p and M^•_{w,cusp} ⊗ Q_p. It is proved from Theorem 6.2.15 and [BP21] Theorem 6.7.3, and Remark 6.2.18 passes from it to RΓ_w by duality.

items.name: Discreteness of p̄^!F̄ and the projection formula for p̄^!
items.statement: Let p̄ : C̄ → X̄ be a proper morphism of schemes of finite type over Z, and F̄ a coherent sheaf on X̄. Then p̄^*F̄ is pseudo-coherent, and both p̄^*F̄ and p̄^!F̄ are discrete objects of D(O_{C̄,■}). For an invertible sheaf L on X̄ there is a projection formula p̄^!(F̄ ⊗ L) ≅ p̄^!F̄ ⊗ p̄^*L.
items.note: This is used without reference in the proof of Proposition 2.3.13 (p. 17): 'using that p̄⋆2F̄ and p̄!1F̄ are discrete', 'Since p̄⋆2F̄ is pseudo coherent', and 'use the projection formula'. In a dynamic compactification the p̄_i are proper but need not have finite Tor-dimension. Checked, the statement is correct. (1) Derived pullback preserves pseudo-coherence, and the solid pullback of a discrete object is the usual derived pullback, which is discrete. (2) For an invertible L, the projection formula for p̄^! follows formally: take right adjoints in p̄_!(G ⊗ p̄^*L^{-1}) ≅ p̄_!G ⊗ L^{-1}. (3) Discreteness of p̄^!F̄. First, f^! is local on the source ((f∘j)^! = j^*f^! for open j), so one may assume f : Spec B → Spec A is affine of finite type. Factor f as a closed immersion i into A^n_A followed by h : A^n_A → Spec A. Then h^! = h^*(−)[n] preserves discrete objects. For a closed immersion into Spec C with C noetherian, i^!N = RHom_C(B, N) is computed from a resolution of B by finite free C-modules. When N is discrete and bounded below (for example a coherent sheaf), this is a bounded-below complex in which each term is a finite sum of terms of N, so it is discrete. Clausen–Scholze (Lectures on Condensed Mathematics, Theorem 8.13(iv)) state only the case f^!A. Neither library has solid quasi-coherent sheaves: Mathlib has only the predicate CondensedMod.IsSolid on condensed modules. The draft roadmap AnalyticStacks covers part of the statement. AS.0 has 'the projection and base-change formulas they satisfy', which gives (2). AS.3 has 'maps of finite Tor-dimension are suave', which gives (3) when p̄ has finite Tor-dimension. No layer states (3) for a general proper map: AS.3 has only 'for proper f, f_* preserves pseudocoherent and coherent objects'.

items.name: Derived limits of essentially zero and Mittag-Leffler systems
items.statement: An essentially zero inverse system of modules has vanishing derived limit. For an inverse system (K_n)_n of complexes there is an exact sequence 0 → lim^1_n H^{i−1}(K_n) → H^i(lim_n K_n) → lim_n H^i(K_n) → 0. So if (H^{i−1}(K_n))_n satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition, then H^i(lim_n K_n) ≅ lim_n H^i(K_n). This holds for inverse systems of finite modules over an artinian ring.
items.note:
Used on p. 16 in the proof of Proposition 2.3.5: '{M[f^n]}_n is an essentially zero inverse system and so its limit is zero', and 'the system {H^i(X̄, 𝓘^n F̄)}_n satisfies the Mittag-Leffler property (since it is a system of finite A-modules), hence H^i(X̄, j_!F) = lim_n H^i(X̄, 𝓘^n F̄)'.

Planned in two layers.
- CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.2: 'Construct the derived inverse limit of complexes and the Milnor exact sequence; exhibit the possible lim¹ term rather than commuting completion and cohomology formally. Prove sufficient surjectivity/Mittag–Leffler criteria at each use.'
- DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P7: 'Work with finite coefficient quotients before inverse limits, prove derived Mittag–Leffler comparisons, and retain lim¹ whenever it does not vanish.'

What the libraries have:
- Mathlib states the Mittag-Leffler condition only for Type-valued cofiltered systems (CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMittagLeffler).
- Neither library has lim¹ or the Milnor exact sequence.
- The Mittag-Leffler property of an inverse system of finite modules over an artinian ring follows from two Mathlib results, applied to the images of the transition maps: isArtinian_of_fg_of_artinian' (a finite module over an artinian ring is artinian) and IsArtinian.monotone_stabilizes (descending chains of submodules stabilise).

In the paper these limits are formed in solid modules. Countable products are exact there, so the same exact sequence holds, and evaluating at a point recovers the classical lim and lim¹ of the underlying modules.

items.name: Local solid computations: products and localizations
items.statement: Let A be a ring of finite type over Z and M̄ a pseudo-coherent object of D((A, A)■). Then M̄ ⊗_{(A,A)■} ∏_{n≥1} A = ∏_{n≥1} M̄; in particular M̄ ⊗_{(A,A)■} A((X^{-1}))/A[X] = M̄[[X^{-1}]]X^{-1} = ∏_{n≥1} M̄X^{-n}. For a discrete A-module M and f ∈ A, the usual tensor product M ⊗_A A[1/f] = colim(M →f M →f ⋯) is already solid, so it computes the solid base change to A[1/f].
items.locator: §2.3.1, proof of Proposition 2.3.2, p. 15; §2.3.7, proof of Proposition 2.3.8, p. 16
items.note:
These are two facts about solid modules, used as the local computations in Propositions 2.3.2 and 2.3.8.
- p. 15, proof of Proposition 2.3.2: 'Since M̄ is pseudo-coherent, we find that M̄ ⊗_{(A,A)■} A((X^{-1}))/A[X] = M̄ ⊗_{(A,A)■} A[[X^{-1}]]X^{-1} = ∏_{n≥1} M̄X^{-n}'.
- p. 16, proof of Proposition 2.3.8: 'We use that if M is discrete the (usual) tensor product M ⊗_A A[1/f] is solid in D(A[1/f]■)'.

Both are planned in the draft roadmap SolidAnalyticRings, which follows Rodríguez Camargo's Notes on solid geometry (arXiv:2603.03012v1).

First fact. SA.3 lists 'Theorem 5.3.2: for R of finite type over Z, R_□[S]=lim_nR[S_n], D(R_□) is the derived category of its heart, and ∏_N R is flat. Propositions 5.3.3, 5.3.7 and 5.3.12'.
- Proposition 5.3.7(4) of those notes is the flatness of ∏_N R. Its proof shows that M ⊗_{R□} ∏_N R = ∏_N M for finitely presented M.
- Remark 5.3.8 states M ⊗^L_{R□} ∏_N R = ∏_N M for every pseudo-compact M.
- A pseudo-coherent M̄ is a bounded above complex of finite free modules. Flatness lets one compute the tensor product termwise, and products are exact, so the formula follows.

Second fact. SA.2 plans analytic rings, 'a full subcategory D(A) ⊆ D(A▷) that is closed under limits and colimits'.
- A[1/f] is itself complete, so every discrete A[1/f]-module, being a colimit of copies of A[1/f], is complete.
- The solid tensor product with A[1/f] = colim(A →f A →f ⋯) commutes with this colimit.

The roadmap works in the light condensed setting, while the paper cites Clausen–Scholze's κ-condensed theory. Only countable products occur here, so the difference does not matter. Mathlib has only the predicate CondensedMod.IsSolid and no solid tensor product.

items.name: Maps from a pseudo-coherent complex into a colimit of uniformly bounded below complexes
items.statement: Let Y be a noetherian scheme, P ∈ D_qc(Y) pseudo-coherent, and (E_n) a filtered system in D_qc(Y) with all E_n in D^{≥a} for one fixed integer a. Then Hom(P, colim_n E_n) = colim_n Hom(P, E_n). Locally P may be replaced by a bounded complex of finite free modules in the relevant range of degrees, and RΓ(Y, −) commutes with filtered colimits of uniformly bounded below complexes.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Proposition 2.3.13, p. 17
items.note:
Used on p. 17 in the proof of Proposition 2.3.13: 'We deduce a map p̄⋆₂F̄ → colim_{n≥0} p̄!₁F̄(nD_C). Since p̄⋆₂F̄ is pseudo coherent, this map factors through a map p̄⋆₂F̄ → p̄!₁F̄(nD_C) for n large enough.'

Why the lower bound matters. On a noetherian scheme the compact objects are the perfect complexes, so for a pseudo-coherent object that is not perfect, Hom(P, −) need not commute with filtered colimits. This lemma supplies what the step needs. The uniform lower bound holds in the application: p̄₁ is proper and F̄ is coherent, so p̄!₁F̄ is bounded below with coherent cohomology, and twisting by the line bundles O(nD_C) does not change the bound.

Proof of the lemma.
- Let E ∈ D^{≥a}, and represent P locally by a bounded above complex of finite free modules.
- The long exact sequence for the stupid truncation gives Hom(P, E) = Hom(σ_{≥a−1}P, E), and σ_{≥a−1}P is perfect.
- The colimit of the E_n again lies in D^{≥a}.
- To globalise, RΓ on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme commutes with filtered colimits. The paper cites this fact as [Sta22], Tag 01FF, for Corollary 2.3.9.

Neither library has pseudo-coherent complexes, D_qc of a scheme, or compact objects of derived categories. No atlas layer states the lemma. Pseudo-coherence over rings appears in DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P7, whose node on perfect complexes has 'equivalently K is pseudo-coherent of finite Tor dimension'. AnalyticStacks AS.1 plans the formalism X ↦ D_qc(X) with the statement of Theorem 8.10 on pseudo-coherent objects. Neither plans this compactness statement.

items.name: Finiteness of Hom between bounded coherent complexes, and splitting of idempotents in D(A)
items.statement: Let A be a noetherian ring and M, N bounded complexes of finitely generated A-modules. Then Hom_{D(A)}(M, N) is a finitely generated A-module; in particular the A-subalgebra of End_{D(A)}(M) generated by one endomorphism T is a finite A-algebra. D(A) has countable direct sums, hence is idempotent complete (Bökstedt–Neeman). So every idempotent e of End_{D(A)}(M) splits, M ≅ eM ⊕ (1 − e)M.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Lemma 2.4.3, p. 18
items.note:
Used on p. 18 in the proof of Lemma 2.4.3: 'We consider the algebra B generated by T in End(M). This is a finite A-algebra. It splits into a product of local A-algebras, B = ∏_i B_i. We have idempotents e_i attached to each B_i and we let M_i = e_iM.' Here End(M) is taken in D(A), so two facts are needed: End_{D(A)}(M) is finite over A, and idempotents split in D(A). Lemma 2.4.3 is then used in Lemma 2.4.4(3) and Lemma 2.4.6 (p. 19) and in Proposition 2.5.4 (p. 20).

What the libraries have (partial only):
- Mathlib proves ModuleCat.finite_ext: Ext^i_R(N, M) is a finite R-module when R is noetherian and N, M are finite. The statement for bounded complexes follows by induction on the number of nonzero cohomology modules, using the truncation triangles and the fact that finite modules over a noetherian ring are closed under submodules, quotients and extensions.
- Mathlib has the notion CategoryTheory.IsIdempotentComplete, but no instance for derived categories.
- Neither library has the Bökstedt–Neeman theorem that a triangulated category with countable coproducts is idempotent complete.

What the atlas plans, for perfect complexes only:
- IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.2: 'For a Hecke action on a bounded perfect complex define its finite image algebras … Prove localization decompositions over complete coefficient rings, support and annihilator lemmas and finite generation'.
- DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P9: 'localize this derived action by idempotents', for a perfect complex.

These layers do not cover Lemma 2.4.3. Its complexes, for example RΓ(X̄, F̄(k₊D₊ − k₋D₋)) in Proposition 2.5.4, are bounded complexes of finite modules over an artinian ring. They need not be perfect, because no flatness is assumed there.

items.name: Tor-independence of schemes over a base
items.statement: Morphisms X → S and S′ → S are Tor-independent if Tor_i^{O_{S,s}}(O_{X,x}, O_{S′,s′}) = 0 for all i > 0 and all points x ∈ X, s′ ∈ S′ lying over the same s ∈ S. Equivalently, the derived fibre product agrees with X ×_S S′, i.e. O_{X×_S S′} = O_X ⊗^L_{O_S} O_{S′}. This holds, for example, when X or S′ is flat over S.
items.locator: Used in §2.6.12 and the proof of Proposition 2.6.13, pp. 22–23 (also in the proof of Lemma 2.2.2, p. 12)
items.note:
Uses in the paper:
- p. 12, proof of Lemma 2.2.2: '(note that C̄ and X are tor-independent)'.
- p. 23, hypothesis of §2.6.12 and Proposition 2.6.13: 'We assume that X and S′ are tor independent and that F is A-flat'.
- p. 23, proof of Proposition 2.6.13, where the hypothesis is used in the form 'By tor independence O_{X′} = O_X ⊗^L_A A′'.

The definition is the standard one (Stacks Project, Tag 08IA). The equivalence with the derived fibre product holds because Tor of the global rings localises to the Tor of local rings at pairs of points over the same point of S. Flatness of either morphism implies Tor-independence.

Mathlib has Tor functors in a monoidal abelian category with projective resolutions (CategoryTheory.Tor), which applies to modules over a commutative ring. Neither library defines Tor-independence of morphisms of schemes or compares the classical and derived fibre products. No atlas layer plans it: DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0 only warns that 'A pushout of ordinary rings without Tor independence is not a derived pushout'.

items.name: Products of copies of R are compact projective solid R-modules
items.statement: Let R be a ring of finite type over Z. For every set I, the product ∏_I R is a compact projective object of the category of solid R-modules (up to isomorphism it is the free solid R-module on a suitable profinite set) (Clausen–Scholze). Consequently every bounded complex whose terms are finite direct sums of such products is a compact object of D(R_■). In particular R̂^I is compact in D(R_■), since Lemma 2.9.2 represents it by a bounded complex with terms R^ℕ.
items.locator: proof of Lemma 2.9.2, p. 27; proof of Lemma 2.9.3, p. 28
items.note:
Used twice, and the paper gives no reference:
- p. 27, proof of Lemma 2.9.2: 'This implies that R̂^{(f₁,…,f_{r−1})} is a compact object in D(R■), represented by a bounded complex, whose terms are of the form R^ℕ'.
- p. 28, proof of Lemma 2.9.3: 'R̂^I is a compact object of D(R■)'.

These uses involve only countable products: R[[X]] ≅ ∏_ℕ R and its solid tensor powers.

Planned in the draft roadmap SolidAnalyticRings, in the light condensed setting.
- SA.1: '∏_N Z is a compact projective generator of Solid'.
- SA.3: 'Theorem 5.3.2: for R of finite type over Z, R_□[S]=lim_nR[S_n] … Propositions 5.3.3, 5.3.7 and 5.3.12'. Taking S = ℕ ∪ {∞} gives R_□[S] = ∏_ℕ R. The proof of Proposition 5.3.7 in Rodríguez Camargo's Notes on solid geometry begins 'The category Mod_{R□} has a compact projective generator given by ∏_N R'.

A bounded complex of compact objects is compact, which gives the consequence for R̂^I. The form for arbitrary index sets I is not planned; it belongs to Clausen–Scholze's κ-condensed theory, where the products ∏_I R are compact projective generators. The uses above need only ∏_ℕ R.

items.name: Hodge–Tate preimage of FL(Q_p) and the position of the Iwahori flag
items.statement: π^{-1}_{HT,K_{p,n}} of the image of FL(Q_p) in |FL|/K_{p,n} is the closure of the ordinary locus 𝒮^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},ord} of 𝒮^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}}. Over π_HT^{-1}(Pw), w ∈ ^MW, one has Lie_A(1) = ⟨e_{w^{-1}(i)} : g+1 ≤ i ≤ 2g⟩ under the trivialization of the Tate module, so these vectors span its multiplicative part. H_{g+i} corresponds to ⟨e_{g+1}, …, e_{g+i}⟩ mod p^n, because K_{p,n} stabilizes this flag mod p^n. Hence over π^{-1}_{HT,K_{p,n}}(w·K_{p,n}), Gr_{g+i} (1 ≤ i ≤ g) is multiplicative if g+i ∈ w^{-1}{g+1, …, 2g} and étale otherwise.
items.note: This item is kept for its first assertion. The paper uses it without proof or reference; the proof of Lemma 4.1.6 (p. 41) opens with 'We know that π^{-1}_{HT,K_{p,n}}(FL(Q_p)) = closure of 𝒮^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},ord}, is the closure of the ordinary locus.' The other assertions are the rest of that proof, which is already recorded with Lemma 4.1.6: Lie_A(1) = ⟨e_{w^{-1}(i)} : g+1 ≤ i ≤ 2g⟩ over π_HT^{-1}(Pw); H_{g+i} ↔ ⟨e_{g+1}, …, e_{g+i}⟩ mod p^n; and the type of each Gr_{g+i}. They were checked by direct computation with the convention w·e_i = e_{w(i)}, which matches w(diag(t)) = diag(t_{w^{-1}(1)}, …). With this convention w^{-1}⟨e_{g+1}, …, e_{2g}⟩ = ⟨e_{w^{-1}(i)} : i ≥ g+1⟩, and B (lower block triangular, with upper triangular diagonal blocks) stabilizes each ⟨e_{g+1}, …, e_{g+i}⟩. The external assertion links the Hodge–Tate period map to the ordinary locus of the Iwahori-level integral model, including its toroidal boundary. One proof goes through the classification of p-divisible groups over O_C by their Hodge–Tate filtration: the filtration Lie_A(1) ⊆ T_p(A) ⊗ C is Q_p-rational exactly when A[p^∞] is an extension of an étale group by a multiplicative one. At the boundary, the abelian part of the semi-abelian degeneration replaces A. No layer plans this. The atlas plans the Siegel Hodge–Tate map (PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S1, S3), but it plans Hodge–Tate fibres only for the unitary data of Caraiani–Scholze. IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.3 reads: 'For a geometric flag point x=Spa(C,O_C)→Fl, identify its polarized p-divisible group over O_C and special fiber X'. Neither library has p-divisible groups.

items.name: Degrees of truncated Barsotti–Tate groups and extreme values of the degree
items.statement: Let V be as in §4.2.7, with v(p) = 1. For a p-divisible group G over V, deg G[p^m] = m·dim G. A truncated Barsotti–Tate group of level n and dimension d has degree nd, in particular a multiple of n. For a finite flat group scheme H of order p^h, 0 ≤ deg H ≤ h. deg H = 0 iff H is étale, and deg H = h iff H is multiplicative, since deg H + deg H^D = h.
items.locator: proofs of Proposition 4.2.8 and Corollary 4.2.10, p. 45; proof of Proposition 4.2.14, p. 46
items.note: This item is kept: these basic properties of Fargues's degree are used without statement. The proof of Proposition 4.2.8 (p. 45) needs deg G[p] = dim G for 'H[p^l]/H[p^{l−1}] is a BT_1 of degree deg H[p] = dim G − deg L'. It needs the same fact, with additivity, for 'deg p^{-1}H = deg H + deg G[p], deg p^{-n}L = deg L + deg G[p^n]'. Corollary 4.2.10 (p. 45) concludes that the groups 'are BT_n's and their degree is a multiple of n'. Proposition 4.2.14 (p. 46) uses 'n ≥ deg p_2^*H_{g+1,x} ≥ deg p_1^*H_{g+1,x} ≥ 0' and reads off étale groups at degree 0 and multiplicative groups at degree n. The bounds 0 ≤ deg H ≤ h and the two extreme cases already follow from facts recorded with Fargues's divisor: D_H + D_{H^D} = V(p^h), and the complement of D_H is the étale locus. The new content is deg H = n·d for a truncated Barsotti–Tate group H of level n and dimension d, because ω_H is free of rank d over V/p^n. This includes deg G[p^m] = m·dim G. Neither library has p-divisible or truncated Barsotti–Tate groups; the library audit finds no p-divisible group in either. No layer plans Fargues's degree. The extraction of Pilloni (Duke 2020) routes the degree to HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0 by a source route (definition, additivity, deg G + deg G^D = height, growth along generic isomorphisms), and BT_n to FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1.

items.name: Conjecture 5.6.1 for w = Id and w = w_0^M in every genus (Remarks 1.4.4 and 5.6.4)
items.statement: For every g ≥ 1, Conjecture 5.6.1 holds for w = Id and for w = w_0^M, the longest element of ^MW (Remark 1.4.4). Remark 5.6.4 says that the same kind of argument as in Proposition 5.6.3 would prove the expected vanishing of RΓ_w(K^p) or RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) for certain particular w and all g, but that the authors could not find a general argument.
items.locator: §5.6, Remark 5.6.4 and the case w = Id in the proof of Proposition 5.6.3, p. 58; Remark 1.4.4, p. 5

prerequisites.citation: P. Scholze (with D. Clausen), Lectures on condensed mathematics, course notes (paper's [CSb]); posted as arXiv:2605.03658 (2026)
prerequisites.why: Lectures VIII–XI (solid quasi-coherent sheaves on schemes, the six-functor formalism and coherent duality) underlie all of §2: D(O_{X,■}) (§2.2, p. 12), proper base change (Lemma 2.2.2), j_!M = M ⊗ A((X^{-1}))/A[X] (Prop. 2.3.2, p. 15), limits and colimits (Lemma 2.4.4), base change of correspondences (§2.6.12), the duality p_*D_X = D_S p_! (Thm 2.7.1) and flat base change (Lemma 2.8.1). The atlas uses only its early lectures (solid abelian groups).

prerequisites.why: All of §6 and the application §1.5: cohomology with support on rigid spaces and Banach sheaves (§6.1.1), potent compactness of T and independence of the finite-slope part from the support (Prop. 6.1.4 = its Thm 5.3.7), Hodge–Tate support conditions (Prop. 6.1.11), lattices and integral models of the locally analytic sheaves (Thm 6.2.9, Props 6.2.12, 6.2.14), vanishing (Cor. 6.2.17), and its Thms 5.12.3, 5.12.5, 5.12.11 for Thm 1.5.1. The paper proves its Conjectures 5.9.2, 5.10.7 and 6.8.1 in the Siegel case. The atlas cites only its §4.4 (the Hodge–Tate period morphism).

Also a prerequisite of PAPER-PILLONI-20.

routes.title: Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology
routes.brief:
Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology (HigherHidaAndColemanTheory; parent PadicFamilies). This paper joins PAPER-PILLONI-20's proposal of this roadmap. The design job merges this brief with PAPER-PILLONI-20's brief into one roadmap.

Where it starts. PadicFamilies stops at ordinary and Coleman families in a single cohomological degree, for modular curves and totally real fields (L0–L5), with L0a's projector and L2a's eigenvariety gluing. PAPER-PILLONI-20's brief starts there and treats the Siegel threefold at Klingen level along one line of weights. This paper extends the same Part II in three directions:
- abstract ordinary cohomology with partial support for dynamic correspondences (§2), the roadmap's new foundation;
- GSp_{2g} for every g at deep Iwahori level, with one theory for each Kostant representative w ∈ ^MW, over the whole weight space (§§4–5);
- the comparison with higher Coleman theory in genus g (§6).

Source: G. Boxer and V. Pilloni, "Higher Hida theory for Siegel modular forms", Invent. Math. 244 (2026) 45–141, doi:10.1007/s00222-025-01393-2. "p. N" is a page of the authors' version of 5 November 2025 (65 pp.). Every E-number here is this paper's sourceIssues entry PAPER-BOXER-PILLONI-26/E<n>. Secondary sources: [BP21] Boxer–Pilloni, Higher Coleman theory (arXiv:2110.10251, cited in that numbering throughout, E114); [BP22] Boxer–Pilloni, Épijournal Géom. Algébrique 6 (2022), the genus-one case; Pilloni, Duke Math. J. 157 (2011).

Final results as printed (pp. 4–6). Setting:
- G = GSp_{2g}; µ is the Hodge cocharacter, P_µ the Siegel parabolic, M_µ its Levi (printed "unipotent radical", E1); T ⊆ B ⊆ P_µ; w_{0,M} and w_0 are the longest elements of W_M and W; d = g(g+1)/2 (E8).
- K^p = ∏_{ℓ≠p} K_ℓ is neat (p. 34); T^sph is the restricted tensor product of the spherical Hecke algebras at the ℓ with K_ℓ = G(Z_ℓ).
- For w ∈ ^MW, RΓ_w(K^p, cusp/∅) ∈ D(Z_p[T(Q_p)] ⊗ T^sph) is the ordinary part of cohomology with w-dependent support on toroidal compactifications of Igusa varieties (§5.2).
- T′(Z_p) is the pro-p subgroup of T(Z_p), Λ′ = Z_p[[T′(Z_p)]], Λ = Z_p[[T(Z_p)]]. A complex in D(Z_p[T′(Z_p)]) is admissible of amplitude [a, b] if it is represented by M^• in degrees [a, b] with M^i ≅ C^0(T′(Z_p), Z_p)^{n_i} (Definition 1.4.1).

Theorem 1.4.3. The cohomologies RΓ_w(K^p, cusp/∅) satisfy:
1. (5.2.7) RΓ_w(K^p, cusp/∅) is admissible.
2. (5.6.3) If g = 1 or g = 2, RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) has amplitude [0, ℓ(w)] and RΓ_w(K^p) has amplitude [ℓ(w), d].
3. (6.2.17) RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p has amplitude [0, ℓ(w)] and RΓ_w(K^p) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p has amplitude [ℓ(w), d].
4. (4.5.5) Let ν ∈ X^⋆(T)^+ and κ = −w_{0,M}w(ν + ρ) − ρ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M_µ,+}. Let K_p = U_{K_p} × T_{K_p} × Ū_{K_p} be a compact open subgroup of G(Q_p) with an Iwahori decomposition, and n ∈ Z_{≥0} with {t ∈ T(Z_p) : t ≡ 1 mod p^n} ⊆ T_{K_p}. Then there is a T(Q_p)-equivariant quasi-isomorphism RHom_{T_{K_p}}(ν, RΓ_w(K^p)) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p(ζ_{p^n})(−ν) = RΓ(S^tor_{K^pK_p}, ω^κ)^{ord} ⊗_{Q_p} Q_p(ζ_{p^n}), and similarly for cuspidal cohomology.
5. (4.5.2) Let κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M,+} and ν = −w^{−1}w_{0,M}(κ + ρ) − ρ for any w ∈ C(κ); take K_p and n as in 4. There is a T(Q_p)-equivariant spectral sequence ⊕_{w∈C(κ), ℓ(w)=a} H^{a+b}(RHom_{T_{K_p}}(ν, RΓ_w(K^p))) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p(ζ_{p^n})(−ν) ⇒ H^{a+b}(S^tor_{K^pK_p}, ω^κ)^{ord} ⊗_{Q_p} Q_p(ζ_{p^n}).

Proposition 1.4.7. Let M^•_w = RHom_{T(Z_p)}(1, RΓ_w(K^p) ⊗̂_{Z_p} Λ) (printed ⊗; E9). For ν = ν_alg χ : T(Z_p) → Z_p(ζ_{p^n})^× with ν_alg ∈ X^⋆(T)^+ and χ of finite order, κ = −w_{0,M}w(ν_alg + ρ) − ρ (printed ν; E10), and K_p as above with T_{K_p} ⊆ ker χ, M^•_w ⊗_{Λ,−ν} Q_p(ζ_{p^n}) = RΓ(S^tor_{K^pK_p}, ω^κ)^{ord} ⊗_{Q_p} Q_p(ζ_{p^n})[χ], [χ] the χ-isotypic part for the diamond operators of T(Z_p)/T_{K_p}; similarly for cuspidal cohomology.

Theorem 1.4.8 (Serre duality; body Theorems 5.5.1–5.5.2). There is a perfect pairing M^•_w ⊗_Λ M^•_{w_{0,M}ww_0,cusp} → Λ[−d] for which the adjoint of t ∈ T(Q_p) is w_0t^{−1} and the adjoint of [K_ℓgK_ℓ] is [K_ℓg^{−1}K_ℓ] (ℓ ≠ p, K_ℓ = G(Z_ℓ), g ∈ G(Q_ℓ)), compatible with classical Serre duality at locally algebraic dominant weights.

Theorem 1.4.9. The slope 0 part of higher Coleman theory canonically identifies with the rational part of higher Hida theory (precise forms: Theorems 6.2.9, 6.2.15).

Theorem 1.4.10. The lower bounds on slopes of [BP21] Conjectures 5.9.2 and 6.8.1 hold (Corollaries 6.2.10, 6.2.16). Consequently, in the Siegel case, "small slope" replaces "strongly small slope" in [BP21] 5.12.3, 5.12.5, 5.12.11, 6.8.4 and 6.9.3(2) (pp. 62, 64; p. 6 also names 5.12.20).

Theorem 1.5.1. Let p | N, Γ = {γ ∈ Sp_{2g}(Z) : γ ≡ 1 mod N}, t_i = diag(p,…,p,1,…,1,p^{−1},…,p^{−1}) with 2i entries 1 (0 ≤ i ≤ g), H^⋆(Γ, Z_p)^{ord} the direct factor on which every [Γt_iΓ] acts invertibly, and H^⋆(Γ, Q_p)^{ord} = H^⋆(Γ, Z_p)^{ord} ⊗ Q_p. Then H^i(Γ, Q_p)^{ord} = 0 for 0 ≤ i < d.

Record as Prop-valued statements, never assumed: Conjecture 5.6.1 (for every g and w, RΓ_w(K^p) is admissible of amplitude [ℓ(w), d] and RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) of amplitude [0, ℓ(w)]) with its equivalent form for M^•_w (Remark 5.6.2; prove the equivalence), Remark 1.5.2, and [BP21] Conjectures 5.9.2, 5.10.7 and 6.8.1 for general abelian-type data. The Siegel cases of these three conjectures are proved here: Corollaries 6.2.10 and 6.2.16 with E126, and Remark 4.3.19. Proposition 5.6.3 proves Conjecture 5.6.1 for g ≤ 2; Remark 1.4.4 asserts it for w ∈ {Id, w_0^M} in every genus (layer I plans the proof); Remark 6.2.18 gives it after inverting p.

Corrections to the final results.
- 1: Proposition 5.2.3 holds only when T(Z_p) normalises K_{p,P}. Build Proposition 5.2.7 from such a K_{p,P}, and prove independence of K_{p,P} as in Proposition 5.2.5 (E106, E107).
- 2: D_{w,+} has the support of Z_{1,<1} (E112). Apply the dimension argument to ω^κ(−cusp)(−kD_{w,−}) on S^tor_{(w−1,w+1)} ∖ D_{w,+} (E113). K^p is a superscript (E98).
- 3 is Corollary 6.2.17 for M^•_w ⊗ Q_p and M^•_{w,cusp} ⊗ Q_p, carried to RΓ_w(K^p) and RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) by the duality of Lemma 5.4.2 (Remark 6.2.18). The proof of Corollary 6.2.17 combines Theorem 6.2.15 with [BP21] Theorem 6.7.3, whose non-cuspidal case rests on the duality of [BP21] Theorem 6.7.2 and whose cuspidal case is [BP21] Theorem 6.6.1; it does not use Theorem 1.4.8. The cuspidal complexes need the cuspidal analogue of Theorem 6.2.15 (E126).
- 4 and 5: C(κ) is defined with dominance in X^⋆(T)_Q (E3). Corollaries 4.5.4–4.5.5 take κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M,+} with C(κ) = {w} (E101). The proof of Theorem 4.5.2 needs the following:
  - extend the filtration by F_{d+1} = S^tor (E102);
  - compare the local terms through Proposition 2.2.11 and Theorem 2.5.1(1) (E100);
  - state Corollary 4.4.3 over p_i^{−1}(Z_{>w−1}) (E103);
  - prove the composition law T_tT_{t′} = T_{tt′} behind the T(Q_p)-action of Proposition 4.4.5 (E99).
- 4 and 5, change of level: points 4 and 5 are printed for an arbitrary K_p with an Iwahori decomposition, but Theorem 4.5.2 and Corollary 4.5.5 are proved on the integral model S^tor of deep Iwahori level K^pK_{p,n}. Its formal strata 𝔖^tor_w are the Igusa formal schemes of level K^pK_{w,p,P} (Lemma 4.1.7), and the proofs use a character χ of T(Z/p^n) and the sheaves ω̃^κ(χ). The paper leaves the passage implicit; layer L plans it in three steps. First, Theorem 5.3.5 and the comparison with §4.4 that follows it identify RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, χ) with RHom_{T(Z_p)}(νχ, RΓ_w(K^p) ⊗ Z_p(ζ_{p^n})). After inverting p, RHom_{T_{K_p}}(ν, RΓ_w(K^p)) ⊗ Q_p(ζ_{p^n}) is the direct sum of the RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, χ) ⊗ Q_p over the characters χ of the finite group T(Z_p)/T_{K_p}. Integrally it need not split, because p can divide the order of that group. Second, invert p in the abutment of Theorem 4.5.2; Corollary 4.5.5 already does this in regular weight. Third, the equality RΓ(S^tor_{K^pK_p}, ω^κ)^{ord} = J_B^{ord}(colim_{K′_p} RΓ(S^tor_{K^pK′_p,Σ}, ω^κ))^{T_{K_p}} of §1.3.4 (with E4) shows that the target depends on K_p only through T_{K_p}.
- Proposition 1.4.7: normalise ν^univ(t) = [t^{−1}] (E110).
- Theorem 1.4.8: the second factor's Λ-structure is twisted by the involution ι of Λ induced by t ↦ w_0t^{−1}. The pairing is M^•_w ⊗_Λ ι^⋆M^•_{w_{0,M}ww_0,cusp} → Λ[−d], and it specialises at (κ, χ) and at (−w_{0,M}κ − 2ρ_nc, w_0χ^{−1}) (E7). The Serre dual in the proof of Theorem 5.5.1 is ω^{−w_{0,M}κ−2ρ_nc}(−D) (E111). The body never states the prime-to-p adjoint; layer H proves it.
- Theorem 1.4.10 (E126): reduce to T^{++} by the cone argument; first state the cuspidal analogues of Theorems 6.2.9 and 6.2.15; then deduce part (2) of each conjecture (characters of T^− on the '−' theories) from part (1) by the Serre duality of [BP21] Theorems 5.7.1–5.7.2 and 6.7.1–6.7.2, with κ^∨ = −2ρ_nc − w_{0,M}κ. Cite [BP21] in one numbering (E114).
- Theorem 1.5.1 is deduced on p. 62 from the small-slope form of [BP21] Theorem 5.12.11. It inherits E126 and the §6.1 repairs E115 and E119.
- p. 2 claims that Pilloni's M^0 → M^1 extends over the weight space. State instead what is proved (E2): M^•_Id and M^•_{w_1} interpolate ordinary H^0 and H^1 in the regular weights with C(κ) = {Id}, resp. {w_1}; in the singular weights ω^{(k,2)} (C(κ) = {Id, w_1}) the Cousin spectral sequence computes ordinary Iwahori-level cohomology from them. No identification with PAPER-PILLONI-20's Klingen-level M is claimed.

Additions, layer by layer. Layers A–C need nothing from PAPER-PILLONI-20's layers and open the merged roadmap. Pilloni's Proposition 7.2.1 and the level comparison in the proof of his Theorem 11.3.1 are analogues of Propositions 2.2.11 and 2.8.2, not cases of them. Proposition 2.2.11 compares dynamic compactifications of one correspondence (C, X), with X̄ ∖ X = D_+ ∪ D_−; Pilloni's 7.2.1 changes the proper model X_Σ itself and rests on his Theorem 6.1.5.1. Proposition 2.8.2 concerns the iterated correspondences C^{(n)} with coefficient O_X; the proof of Pilloni's 11.3.1 passes through Klingen level p^m and the sheaves F^k_{m,1}. Both stay where PAPER-PILLONI-20's brief plans them (its layers 2 and 5).

A. Compactified and dynamic correspondences; cohomology with partial support (§§2.1.7–2.3, pp. 7–17).
- Definition 2.1.9 with maps and strict maps, Lemmas 2.1.11–2.1.13; D ≤ sD′ (Definition 2.1.15(2)), Lemma 2.1.17, Example 2.1.21; strictly and compactly expanded or contracted subschemes (Definition 2.1.19(2),(3),(5),(6)).
- Dynamic, strict and compact dynamic correspondences and compactifications (Definitions 2.1.24, 2.1.26, 2.1.28), Lemmas 2.1.29–2.1.35.
- RΓ_{D+,D−} and RΓ_{D−,D+} (Definition 2.2.4), Lemmas 2.2.6–2.2.8, T_𝒞 (Propositions 2.2.10–2.2.11), Corollary 2.3.11, Proposition 2.3.13, Corollary 2.3.14. Prove that T_𝒞 for D± = ∅ is IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes' action on RΓ(X, F).
- Corrections: the equaliser step for cofilteredness (E14); n_0 ≥ 1 (E15); p̄_1^⋆D ≤ (1/p)p̄_2^⋆D in Example 2.1.21 (E16); E17; Cartier pull-backs in Lemma 2.1.30 (E18); E19; E20; the second chain of Proposition 2.2.10 (E21); Proposition 2.2.11 for a strict map 𝒞′ → 𝒞 (E22); the compatibility of α± with s_+, t_− in Corollary 2.3.14 (E25); uniformly bounded-below targets in Proposition 2.3.13 (E26).

B. Ordinary parts and ordinary cohomology (§§2.4–2.8, pp. 17–27).
- M^ord = M ⊗^L_{(A[T],A)■} A[T,T^{−1}]■ (Definition 2.4.2), Lemmas 2.4.3–2.4.4, finite rank (Definition 2.4.5, Lemma 2.4.6). Prove that Lemma 2.4.3's summand is PadicFamilies L0a's eM on finite modules.
- Theorem 2.5.1 and RΓ(X, F)^{C−ord}, Lemma 2.5.3, Proposition 2.5.4.
- Propositions 2.6.2 and 2.6.13, Theorems 2.6.8 and 2.6.10. The base change of strict dynamic compactifications along S′ → S is proved here; T ⊗ 1, the coinvariant descent, Lemma 2.6.11 and T′ are imported.
- Proposition 2.7.2, the transpose 𝒞^t, Theorem 2.7.4; §2.8 (C^{(n)}, Lemma 2.8.1, T_n, square (2.8.A), Proposition 2.8.2).
- Corrections: stable ∞-categories (E28) with the shifts of E23; Lemma 2.4.4 also for lim–colim (E27); E29–E32; in Proposition 2.6.13, X and C Tor-independent from S′ over S (E35); E36; E38; a strict dynamic compactification in §2.8 (E37); E39.

C. Compact dynamic correspondences and control theorems (§§2.10–2.11, pp. 29–33).
- Lemma 2.10.2, Propositions 2.10.3 and 2.10.4(1)–(5), the §2.11 setting, Remarks 2.11.2–2.11.3, Theorem 2.11.4(1)–(4) with its three proof steps.
- Corrections: a scheme structure on Y containing U scheme-theoretically (E43, E46); Proposition 2.10.3 for F bounded below with coherent cohomology, T factoring through τ^{≥a} (E45), interiors in C̄ (E47); the §2.11 inclusions p̄_2^⋆D′_+ ⊆ p̄_1^⋆D″_+ and p̄_1^⋆D′_− ⊆ p̄_2^⋆D″_− (E48); target RΓ(X, F)^{C−ord} in Theorem 2.11.4(3) (E49); E50.

Addition to PAPER-PILLONI-20's layer 1. Genus-g classical Hida theory (p. 2): p-adic modular forms on the ordinary Igusa tower of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentrationPartIISiegelOrdinary, injectivity of restriction, control, and finite projectivity of the cuspidal ordinary part over Z_p[[T(Z_p)]]. Prove that at g = 2 these forms agree with SiegelModularFormsModPn's p-adic Siegel modular forms; the genus-two statements of PAPER-PILLONI-20's layer 1 then become instances.

D. Ordinarity in weight κ (§1.3.4, p. 3). v(χ) ∈ X^⋆(T)_R; Definition 1.3.5; J_B^{ord}; RΓ(S^tor_{K^pK_p}, ω^κ)^{ord} and its equality with J_B^{ord}(colim_{K′_p} RΓ(S^tor_{K^pK′_p,Σ}, ω^κ))^{T_{K_p}}, K^p fixed (E4). The Katz–Mazur inequality v(χ) ≥ −ν ([BP21] Conjecture 5.10.7) is Prop-valued; layer F proves the Siegel case (Remark 4.3.19).

E. Iwahori-level strata, divisors and Hecke correspondences (§§4.1–4.2, pp. 40–46).
- S^tor_{F_p,w}, Remark 4.1.4, 𝔖^tor_w, π_{HT,K_{p,n}}, Lemmas 4.1.6–4.1.7 with the Hodge–Tate preimage of FL(Q_p) from Lemma 4.1.6's proof; D_i, Lemma 4.1.9, Z_k, Proposition 4.1.13, Corollary 4.1.14, the convention S^tor = S̃^tor, Remark 4.1.15, Z_{>w−1}, Lemma 4.1.17, F_i, Lemma 4.1.18.
- C^tor_t, the normalisation of S^tor × S^tor in C^tor_{t,Q_p}, stays here because S^tor is this layer's blow-up. Also Lemma 4.2.2, 𝔆^tor_{t,w}, Proposition 4.2.4, §4.2.5, Remark 4.2.6, §4.2.7, Proposition 4.2.8, Corollary 4.2.10, Lemmas 4.2.11–4.2.13, Propositions 4.2.14–4.2.15.
- Corrections: n ≥ 1 (E64); D_i along the boundary, with D_i + D_{2g+1−i} = V(p^n) proved there from the imported fact that no irreducible component of the special fibre lies in the boundary (E67); Z_i = Σ_{k≤i} D_{g+k} (E71); in Proposition 4.1.13(2), emptiness only in the special fibre (E70) and an open immersion on the final blow-up only for k ∈ {g−1, g} (E72); the index j = −1 (E76); Corollary 4.2.10 and Proposition 4.2.15 through degrees alone (E77, E81); E68, E69, E73–E75, E78–E80, E82, E83.

F. Normalised integral correspondences at p (§4.3, pp. 46–49).
- Lemma 4.3.4; K_{p,1,n} and its normalised model; Lemma 4.3.6; O(χ), ω^κ(χ); Lemma 4.3.8; Propositions 4.3.9, 4.3.11, 4.3.13 and Remark 4.3.12; ω̃^κ and Lemma 4.3.14; Lemma 4.3.16, Propositions 4.3.17–4.3.18, ω̃^κ(χ); Remark 4.3.19.
- Corrections: sums to g (E85); the second assertion of Lemma 4.3.6 via the torsor of trivialisations (E86); E87; D_{2g+1−i} (E88); E89.

G. Higher Hida complexes in fixed weight; the Cousin complex (§§4.4–4.5, pp. 49–53).
- S^tor_{F_p,(w−1,w+1)}, D_{w,±}, Lemma 4.4.2, Corollary 4.4.3, Proposition 4.4.4; RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ) with its χ and cuspidal variants; Proposition 4.4.5, Remark 4.4.6.
- Theorem 4.5.2, Corollaries 4.5.4–4.5.5, Proposition 4.5.8. The Cousin spectral sequence on S^tor instantiates the imported Theorem 2.9.7 and Proposition 2.9.9; check p_1 proper (E42).
- Corrections: Z_{i,>w_i−1} (E90); D_{w,−} = ∪_i Z_{i,>w_i}, D_{w,+} = ∪_i Z_{i,<w_i} (E91); E92–E103; E105.

H. Higher Hida theory in families (§§5.1–5.5, pp. 53–57). This generalises PAPER-PILLONI-20's layer 5 and does not replace it.
- Decomposable K_{p,P} ⊆ P′(Q_p), Remarks 5.1.1–5.1.3, the Igusa Hecke correspondences for t ∈ T_w(Q_p)^{++}, Theorem 5.1.4; Lemma 5.2.2, RΓ_w(K^pK_{p,P}), Propositions 5.2.3, 5.2.5, 5.2.7, RΓ_w(K^p), the w-twisted action.
- The T^sph-action, which the paper uses but never constructs. For ℓ ≠ p with K_ℓ = G(Z_ℓ), build the prime-to-p Hecke correspondences on IG^tor_{K^pK_{p,P}} from the K^p-level structure of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentrationPartIISiegelOrdinary and the toroidal Hecke maps of ShimuraCompactifications C3. Prove that they preserve D_{w,±} and commute with the T_w(Q_p)^{++}-correspondences, so that T^sph acts on RΓ_w(K^pK_{p,P}) and RΓ_w(K^p), commuting with T(Q_p). In Theorem 5.5.2, prove that the adjoint of [K_ℓgK_ℓ] is [K_ℓg^{−1}K_ℓ].
- §5.3: fixed weight at decomposable level, Proposition 5.3.3, the lowest-weight projection and the vanishing of its kernel's ordinary part, Theorem 5.3.5, RΓ_w(K^p, κ, χ), comparison with layer G.
- §5.4: Λ, M^•_w, Lemmas 5.4.1–5.4.2, Remark 5.4.3, T_w and E_w = Spec T_w (instances of IHG.2). §5.5: Theorems 5.5.1–5.5.2.
- Corrections: t_0^nK_{p,P}t_0^{−n} ⊆ P′(Z_p) (E104); E106–E111; E7–E10.

I. GSp_4 and the amplitude conjecture (§5.6, p. 58).
- Conjecture 5.6.1, Remark 5.6.2, Proposition 5.6.3 for g = 1 and g = 2, and the cases w ∈ {Id, w_0^M} in every genus.
- For g = 2, import the spherical two-affine covering of the p-rank ≥ 1 locus and Ha on 𝔛^⋆ from SiegelModularFormsModPn. Prove only the Iwahori-level clauses: the w = Id Igusa component maps into the ordinary locus, and S^tor_{(w−1,w+1)} ∖ D_{w,+} lies in the p-rank ≥ 1 locus.
- In genus g the case w = Id needs the ordinary locus of the special fibre of the minimal compactification to be affine. Plan this here for every g, as the non-vanishing locus of Ha descended to the minimal compactification, a section of a power of the Hodge line bundle, which is ample there by ShimuraCompactifications C5. Ha is imported from HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0, which owns the Hasse invariant of a BT_1 over any F_p-scheme. SiegelModularFormsModPn's genus-two statement is the case g = 2.
- Check Lan's Definition 8.5 for the Igusa sheaves, so that IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes' form of [Lan17] Theorem 8.6 applies.
- Corrections: E112, E113, E98.

J. Support conditions and finite slope parts (§6.1, pp. 58–61).
- [BP21] higher Coleman theory in the Siegel case. This generalises PAPER-PILLONI-20's layers 6–7 and does not replace them. Plan the statements the paper uses, with their [BP21] hypotheses and the [BP21] results they rest on, in the numbering of arXiv:2110.10251 (E114):
  - Banach sheaves on rigid spaces (Definition 2.5.2), compact maps (Definition 2.5.3) and cohomology with support as projective systems of Banach complexes (Lemma 2.5.21). No atlas stage plans them;
  - Corollary 3.3.14, Lemmas 3.4.1 and 3.5.10(5), using Lemma 3.1.2 (X^w ⊆ Y_w) from ShimuraData D3; Theorem 5.3.7, for the slope decompositions of LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4;
  - Theorems 5.7.1–5.7.2, Lemma 5.9.10, Definitions 5.11.2 and 5.11.14 (small and strongly small slope), Theorems 5.12.3, 5.12.5, 5.12.11 and 5.12.20;
  - Lemma 6.3.10, the formal models in the proof of Lemma 6.6.2, Theorems 6.6.1 and 6.7.1–6.7.3, Corollary 6.8.4 and Theorem 6.9.3(2).
- Definition 6.1.3, RΓ_{m,n}, Proposition 6.1.4, Lemma 6.1.5, Corollary 6.1.6, Proposition 6.1.7.
- 𝒰_{≥w−ε}, 𝒰_{≤w+ε}, 𝒵_{<w+ε}, 𝒵_{>w−ε}; Propositions 6.1.9–6.1.11; the tubes ]X_w[, ]Y_w[ and their π_{HT,K_{p,n}}-preimages; the comparison of the degree and Hodge–Tate finite slope parts.
- Corrections: the intersection pair in Proposition 6.1.7 (E115); E114; E116–E121.

K. Integral overconvergent cohomology and the comparison (§6.2, pp. 61–64). This generalises PAPER-PILLONI-20's layer 8 (M† against M ⊗ Q_p).
- Fixed weight: ε, ε′; Propositions 6.2.2–6.2.3, 6.2.5–6.2.7; RΓ^{int}; Theorem 6.2.9 with [BP21] Lemma 5.9.10 from layer J; Corollary 6.2.10 and the small-slope improvements.
- Families: 𝒯_n, ℐ𝒲_n, κ_A; 𝔉^{ν_A}, 𝔉^{ν_A,n}, built on the Igusa torsors by OverconvergentAutomorphicForms O1's construction, as PAPER-PILLONI-20's brief builds 𝔏^{κ_A}; Propositions 6.2.12–6.2.14 with [BP21] Lemma 6.3.10 and the formal models of layer J; RΓ^{int} in families and in fixed weight; Theorem 6.2.15, Corollary 6.2.16, the small-slope forms of [BP21] Corollary 6.8.4 and Theorem 6.9.3(2), Corollary 6.2.17 from [BP21] Theorem 6.7.3, Remark 6.2.18.
- Corrections: Proposition 6.2.3(2)–(3), second halves, as inclusions of supports (E122); w_i for w_j (E123); Q-Cartier divisors (E124); 𝒰_{≥w−ε} (E125); a lattice in each slope ≤ h part (E127); E126; E128–E133; E110.

L. Main theorems (§1, pp. 2–6).
- Theorems 1.4.3, 1.4.8–1.4.10, Proposition 1.4.7; Remark 1.3.2 (independence of the support condition, made precise by Proposition 2.10.4(5) and Theorem 2.11.4); §1.5 and Theorem 1.5.1; Remark 1.5.2 ([Ven17] §4.2).
- The passage from the Iwahori level K^pK_{p,n} (Igusa level K^pK_{w,p,P}) to an arbitrary K_p with an Iwahori decomposition in points 4 and 5 of Theorem 1.4.3 (see the corrections to 4 and 5).
- The genus-one theory of [BP22] and Grossi's Hilbert theory (p totally split).
- Pilloni's M^0 → M^1 is PAPER-PILLONI-20's Theorem 1.1, already in the roadmap: merge, do not plan twice.

Operators at p. This roadmap owns the normalised Iwahori-level correspondences t, t_w and t̃ (§§4.3, 5.2, 6.2), as it owns PAPER-PILLONI-20's Klingen-level operators. IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes owns the notion of a cohomological correspondence and p_2^⋆ω^κ[1/p] ≅ p_1^⋆ω^κ[1/p]. AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension owns fundamental classes of lci correspondences.

Imports, proposals (all upstream):
- Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes (IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes):
  - the solid cohomological correspondence T: p_2^⋆F → p_1^!F and expanded or contracted subschemes (Definition 2.1.19(1),(4));
  - T ⊗ 1, G-coinvariant descent with Lemma 2.6.11, the finite Tor-independent base change T′, the transpose (Proposition 2.7.3), and Proposition 2.9.9;
  - M_dR, V_κ, ω^κ, Lan's vanishing ([Lan17] Theorem 8.6).
- Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: integral models and reduction (ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII): the interior Iwahori-level model S_{K^pK_{p,n}}, the flag H_i and Gr_i over the interior (E66), and A_{g,δ}.
- Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry, Part II: integral boundary charts of Hodge type (ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary): the toroidal Iwahori-level model S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}}; the chain of semi-abelian schemes, with quasi-finite flat kernels along the boundary; and the fact that no irreducible component of the special fibre lies in the boundary, which layer E uses for D_i + D_{2g+1−i} = V(p^n) (E67).
- Igusa varieties, compactified period fibers and torsion concentration, Part II: ordinary Igusa formal schemes of Siegel varieties (IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentrationPartIISiegelOrdinary): IG_{K^p} with its K^p-level structure, J_ord, P′(Q_p), K_{p,P}, Proposition 3.4.9, Igusa Hecke correspondences, IG^tor, Lemma 3.4.24. PAPER-PILLONI-20's layer 3 reuses this tower only where its Klingen towers over the p-rank ≥ 1 locus meet the ordinary locus. SiegelModularFormsModPn should build its genus-two p-adic Siegel modular forms on this tower rather than on a tower of its own.
- Algebraic modular forms, reduction and Serre weights, Part II: Siegel modular forms of genus two modulo p^n (SiegelModularFormsModPn), for layer I and for the genus-two comparison in the addition to PAPER-PILLONI-20's layer 1.

Imports, draft roadmaps:
- Six-functor formalisms and analytic stacks (AnalyticStacks) AS.0, AS.2, AS.3, including this paper's additions to AS.3, which should form their own substage: supports and Lemma 2.10.1, the Cousin spectral sequence (Theorem 2.9.7), j_! and j_⋆ as limit and colimit of twists (Propositions 2.3.2, 2.3.8), the Hartshorne comparison, and Theorem 2.7.1.
- Light condensed mathematics, solid abelian groups and analytic rings (SolidAnalyticRings) SA.2, SA.3.

Imports, atlas: Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions (PadicFamilies) L0a, L2a; Adic coefficients and comparison with schemes (AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons) L2; Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations) SF.0, SF.2; Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra) P7; Integral Hecke actions, determinants and interpolation (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants) IHG.2; Completed cohomology, homology and arithmetic towers — Part II (CompletedCohomologyPartII) CC.2, CC.3 (admissible complexes and their duality); P-adic measures, completed group algebras, and characteristic ideals (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras) L0, L0a, L1; Shimura data, Hermitian domains, and adelic level structures (ShimuraData) D3 (general ^MW, the M-dominant cone, the involution, Bruhat cells, Schubert varieties, X^w ⊆ Y_w), D5 (GSp_{2g} roots, ρ, ρ_nc, ^MW with the order of E53, (w_i)); Automorphic forms on reductive groups (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups) AF.1, AF.4 (C(κ)); Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) SR.1, SR.2 (Jacquet module, Casselman's lifting); Reductive groups, Part II: local structure and arithmetic models (ReductiveGroupsPartII) RG2.3, RG2.4; Hodge–Tate theory, canonical subgroups, and automorphic period maps (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups) T0 (Fargues's degree and divisor, and the divisor det Lie(f) of an isogeny f of semi-abelian schemes, from which layer E defines D_i along the boundary (E67); the Hasse invariant of a BT_1, for layer I); Shimura towers and perfectoid representability (PerfectoidShimuraVarieties) S1, S3; Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry (ShimuraCompactifications) C2–C5 (C3 for the prime-to-p Hecke maps, C5 for the ample Hodge line bundle on the minimal compactification); Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry) R09.1, R09.7a (separation of two Cartier divisors, stated for arbitrary schemes), A0-extension; Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory) R07.1; Adic Spaces PartII (AdicSpacesPartII), stages "Formal schemes, generic fibres, and Hasse domains" and "Coherent sheaves and finite traces" (the formal–rigid comparison of coherent cohomology on quasi-compact non-proper opens); Locally analytic distributions, growth, and character spaces (LocallyAnalyticDistributions) L3, L4; Overconvergent Hilbert modular forms and p-adic automorphic coefficients (OverconvergentAutomorphicForms) O1, O8 (the equivariant-sheaf construction and its genus-g Siegel instance); Arithmetic locally symmetric spaces and their cohomology (ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces) ALS.1, ALS.3 (the Γ(N) double cosets).

This roadmap never imports GSp4NonregularModularityLifting, and no upstream proposal above imports this roadmap.

Consumers: those of PAPER-PILLONI-20's brief, GSp4NonregularModularityLifting and AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity (pending).

Acceptance tests:
- #^MW = 2^g, ℓ(w_{0,M}ww_0) = d − ℓ(w), and for g = 2 the lengths are 0, 1, 2, 3. Theorem 1.4.8 with E7 exchanges the amplitudes [ℓ(w), d] and [0, ℓ(w_{0,M}ww_0)] of Conjecture 5.6.1.
- g = 1: RΓ_Id(K^p) and RΓ_Id(K^p, cusp) sit in degree 0, and the w_0^M theories in degree 1 ([BP22]).
- Frobenius on X̄ over F_p strictly contracts every closed subscheme with s = 1/p, and p̄_2^⋆D = p·p̄_1^⋆D for D locally principal (E16).
- For X proper, D_± = ∅ and A artinian, RΓ(X, F)^{C−ord} is L0a's ordinary summand of RΓ(X, F) for IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes' T.
- For n = 1 the strata S^tor_{F_p,w} cover the ordinary locus; for n ≥ 2 they do not (Remark 4.1.4). D_i + D_{2g+1−i} = V(p^n) holds on all of S^tor (E67).
- H^0(Γ, Q_p)^{ord} = 0 directly: [Γt_0Γ] acts on H^0(Γ, Z_p) = Z_p by its degree, a positive power of p.

routes.title: Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes
routes.brief:
This entry joins the Part II that PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 (CG18) proposes and PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 (CG20) and PAPER-PILLONI-20 (PILLONI-20) join, under the same id, parent (Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, AutomorphicBundles) and title; the design job merges the four briefs. The roadmap starts where AutomorphicBundles B3–B5 stop; its layers are CG18's 1–4 and CG20's 5–8. Source: G. Boxer and V. Pilloni, "Higher Hida theory for Siegel modular forms", Invent. Math. 244 (2026) 45–141, doi:10.1007/s00222-025-01393-2. Pages are those of the authors' version of 5 November 2025 (printed page = PDF page). sourceIssues are PAPER-BOXER-PILLONI-26's.

Results as printed, with corrections.
- Proposition 2.9.9 (pp. 28–29). Let (C, X, p₁, p₂) be a correspondence, T: p₂^⋆F → p₁^!F a cohomological correspondence, and Z₋₁ = ∅ ⊆ Z₀ ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ Z_d = X closed subschemes. "Assume that p₁^⋆(Z_l) ⊆ p₂^⋆(Z_l) for all 0 ≤ l ≤ d (set theoretically). Then we have an action of T on RΓ(Ẑ_l, F), RΓ_c(U_l, F) and RΓ_c(Ẑ_l ∖ Ẑ_{l−1}, F) for all i, compatible with the natural morphisms. The spectral sequence of theorem 2.9.7 is T-equivariant."
  - Read "for all 0 ≤ l ≤ d" for "for all i" (E41).
  - Add that p₁ is proper. T then acts on RΓ(X, G), for G = (j_l)_!j_l^⋆F, F or (î_l)_⋆î_l^⋆F, by pullback along p₂, the map of triangles, and the trace (p₁)_!p₁^! → Id (E42).
  - The spectral-sequence clause needs F ∈ D^−(O_{X,■}), as Theorem 2.9.7 does.
  - In the proof, the immersions C_{U_l,k} ↪ C land in C, and (j_l)_! replaces (j_l)_⋆ twice (E44).
- Proposition 2.7.3 (pp. 23–24). For C, X smooth over S, F locally free of finite rank and T: p₂^⋆F → p₁^!F, "Applying D_C to T we obtain a transpose of the cohomological correspondence: T^t: p₁^⋆D_X(F) → p₂^!D_X(F)", for (C, X, p₂, p₁).
- Lemma 2.6.11 (p. 22). "Let r: Y → X be a finite étale cover with group G, then r_⋆O_Y is a finite locally projective sheaf of O_X[G]-modules. If furthermore X → Spec A is flat, then r_⋆O_Y [is] A[G]-flat" (E34).
- §1.1 (p. 2). For κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M_µ,+}, colim_K RΓ(S^tor_{K,Σ}, ω^κ) and its cuspidal counterpart "are independent of the choice of Σ. They are complexes of smooth admissible G(A_f)-representations, and if we tensor with C, these cohomologies can be computed by automorphic forms by [Su24]." Here [Su24] is J. Su, "Coherent cohomology of Shimura varieties and automorphic forms", Ann. Sci. Éc. Norm. Supér. (4) 57 (2024), no. 4, 1039–1099. M_µ is the Levi of P_µ, not its unipotent radical (E1).
- §1.3.3 (p. 3). For κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M_µ,+} and w ∈ C(κ), ν + ρ = −w^{−1}w_{0,M}(κ + ρ) "is the dominant representative of the infinitesimal character of automorphic forms contributing to the coherent cohomology in weight κ". C(κ) imposes dominance in X^⋆(T)_Q (E3).
- §1.3.7 (p. 4). For κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M_µ,+}, w ∈ C(κ) and π_∞(κ, w) as in Theorem 1.3.8: "Let π = π_∞(κ, w) ⊗ π_f be an automorphic representation. Then π_f ↪ colim_K H^{ℓ(w)}(S^tor_{K,Σ}, ω^κ) ⊗ C." Read "cuspidal automorphic representation" (E6). In degree 0 the embedding, and the following sentence on w = Id, hold for every automorphic π (E6). π_∞(κ, w) is determined by κ and w, not by ℓ(w) (E5).

Additions, by layer.

Layer 1.
- The M-torsor M_dR (§4.3.1, p. 46) of triples (ψ₁, ψ₂, c) with ψ₂ = c(ψ₁^t)^{−1}. It frames the graded pieces ω_{A^t} and Lie_A of the logarithmic de Rham sequence 0 → ω_{A^t} → H_{1,dR}(A) → Lie_A → 0 (CG20's integral Hodge sequence, in logarithmic form). Also plan the functor from representations of M on finitely generated Z_p-modules to Coh(S^tor), which gives locally free sheaves on finite free ones. State it for any Z_p-scheme carrying a semi-abelian scheme A, a semi-abelian dual A^t and a polarization λ: A → A^t of degree prime to p (principal for the paper's A = A_g, where d_0 = 1). The identification ω_{A^t} ≅ ω_A through λ is what gives ψ₂ = c(ψ₁^t)^{−1} its meaning. Prove the construction compatible with pullback. Instances:
  - the Iwahori-level toroidal models S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} of Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry, Part II: integral boundary charts of Hodge type (ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary), with A = A_g. Their open parts are the models of Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: integral models and reduction (ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII).
  - Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology (HigherHidaAndColemanTheory) pulls M_dR back to its blow-ups.
- V_κ, a dual Weyl module, with (m′·f)(m) = f(m′^{−1}m) (E84); ω^κ = π_⋆O_{M_dR}[−w_{0,M}κ] and its dependence on A and V_κ (Remark 4.3.2, pp. 46–47).
  - For the Siegel datum, M_dR is the Levi torsor from which Lan–Suh build CG20's bundles W^can_µ. Plan one torsor and one functor. Obtain W^can_µ and ω^κ as its values on the respective lattices, and W^sub_µ = W^can_µ(−D) and ω^κ(−D) as their twists by O(−D). Prove W^can_µ ≅ ω^κ for the matching weight whenever the lattices agree.
  - Also prove that π_⋆O_{M_dR}[−w_{0,M}κ], with B ∩ M acting on M_dR by right translation, is the sheaf the functor attaches to V_κ, not to its dual.
- Remark 4.3.3's normalization, with a conversion theorem to B4's Siegel weights, CG20's ω(a,b) and PILLONI-20's Ω^{(k,r)}.

Layer 2. Lemma 2.6.11 is the sheaf form of the projectivity behind CG18's Nakajima lemma. Plan them together, with one proof that r_⋆O_Y is locally projective over O_X[G].

Layer 3. PILLONI-20's quasi-coherent correspondences on schemes become the discrete case of one solid notion.
- Correspondences on p-adic formal schemes are covered too: 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p) in PILLONI-20's §15.1 is the completion Û along p of an open U. They become the case of objects on U in the essential image of î_⋆î^⋆, for î: Û → U. For pseudo-coherent F, Lemma 2.9.3 identifies î_⋆î^⋆F with lim_n F ⊗ O_U/p^n. Prove that on these objects the solid correspondences are PILLONI-20's.
- Cohomological correspondences (§2.2.9, p. 14; §2.3.12, p. 17): T: p₂^⋆F → p₁^!G in D(O_{C,■}), for F, G ∈ D(O_{X,■}), a correspondence as in Definition 2.1.8 and the solid six functors of AnalyticStacks AS.3. Also allow p₂: C → X and p₁: C → Y with different targets, as the pullbacks below need. Prove, or import from AS.3, that the solid p₁^! agrees with A0-extension's upper shriek on bounded-below complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology.
- Expanded and contracted closed subschemes (Definition 2.1.19(1),(4), Remark 2.1.20, p. 9), for any correspondence. They are inclusions of the underlying sets of p₂^{−1}D and p₁^{−1}D. The strict and compact variants stay in HigherHidaAndColemanTheory.
- Strata and completions.
  - The setting of §2.9.8.
  - The map of localization triangles in its proof. Its left map comes from base change, T, C_{U_l,2} ⊆ C_{U_l,1} and the counit for p′₁: C_{U_l,1} → U_l.
  - Proposition 2.9.9 as corrected.
  - Construct the maps p₂^⋆(j_l)_!j_l^⋆F → p₁^!(j_l)_!j_l^⋆F functorially in l, as a map of filtered objects in the stable ∞-category D(O_{C,■}). T then acts on the filtered complex l ↦ RΓ_c(U_l, F), and its actions on the graded pieces RΓ_c(Ẑ_l ∖ Ẑ_{l−1}, F) and the T-equivariance of the spectral sequence follow by functoriality. A separate map of triangles for each l does not determine them, because maps on cones are not unique.
- Coefficient changes, without the strict dynamic compactification the paper assumes:
  - T ⊗ 1 on F ⊗_A M (§2.6.1, p. 21; F ⊗^L_A M = F ⊗_A M, E32), for F a quasi-coherent A-flat sheaf (coherent in the paper) and M finitely generated. This is the general form of reduction modulo p^n.
  - Descent to F/I_G of a G-equivariant T in D(O_C[G]_■), for G finite abelian and F flat over A[G] (§2.6.9, p. 22).
  - Pullback along a Tor-independent square. Take T: p₂^⋆F → p₁^!G with p₁: C → Y, and g: Y′ → Y such that the square formed by C′ = C ×_{p₁,Y,g} Y′, g′: C′ → C and p′₁: C′ → Y′ is Tor-independent (for example, g flat).
    - T′: (p₂g′)^⋆F → (p′₁)^!g^⋆G is g′^⋆T followed by the base-change map g′^⋆p₁^!G → (p′₁)^!g^⋆G. That map is adjoint to (p′₁)_!g′^⋆p₁^!G ≅ g^⋆(p₁)_!p₁^!G → g^⋆G (base change, then the counit).
    - For g finite it can also be obtained from p₁^!g_⋆ ≃ g′_⋆(p′₁)^!. It does not come from the flat base change of D. Clausen and P. Scholze, "Lectures on condensed mathematics" (course notes), Prop. 11.4, which the paper cites there (E35).
    - For g flat it is an isomorphism, the flat base change that §2.8 cites from the same notes.
    - Instances: the base change along a finite S′ → S of §2.6.12 (pp. 22–23), assuming X and C Tor-independent from S′ over S (E35); and the iterated correspondences T_n of §2.8 (p. 25), which HigherHidaAndColemanTheory builds.
  - The twist of T by a map α: p₂^⋆E → p₁^⋆E of locally free sheaves of finite rank. This is T ⊗ α: p₂^⋆(F ⊗ E) → p₁^!(G ⊗ E), through p₁^!(G) ⊗ p₁^⋆E = p₁^!(G ⊗ E).
    - Line bundles occur in Corollary 2.3.14, Proposition 4.3.13 and Lemma 4.3.14.
    - ω^κ over C_{t,Q_p}, with T a fundamental class, occurs in Propositions 4.3.9 and 4.3.11.
- The transpose (Proposition 2.7.3).
  - Add: for X proper over S = Spec A (so that p₁ and p₂ are proper), the duality RHom(RΓ(X, F), A) = RΓ(X, D_X(F)) of Theorem 2.7.1 identifies the endomorphism of RΓ(X, D_X(F)) given by T^t with the dual of the endomorphism of RΓ(X, F) given by T. That duality is AnalyticStacks AS.3's, and layer 1's Serre duality for coherent F.
  - CG18's trace pairing for T_γ and CG20's Hecke-twisted Serre duality are to be derived as instances.
  - The partial-support form used in Theorem 2.7.4 stays in HigherHidaAndColemanTheory.
- The isomorphism p₂^⋆ω^κ[1/p] ≅ p₁^⋆ω^κ[1/p], from p₁^⋆M_dR = p₂^⋆M_dR (p. 47).
  - State it for any correspondence over Z_p whose generic fibre carries a quasi-isogeny p₁^⋆A → p₂^⋆A that respects the polarizations up to a scalar.
  - On the canonical model it agrees with B5's coefficient identification along Hecke correspondences.
  - HigherHidaAndColemanTheory applies it to C_t and proves Lemma 4.3.4.
- The smooth admissible G(A_f)-action over Q on both colimits of §1.1, with K-invariants RΓ(S^tor_{K,Σ}, −), compatible with this layer's Hecke operators. Independence of Σ comes from ShimuraCompactifications C3.
  - In particular, for every compact open K_p, C_c(K_p\G(Q_p)/K_p, Q) acts on RΓ(S^tor_{K^pK_p,Σ}, ω^κ) and on its base change to Q_p.
  - This includes the operators [K_p t K_p], t ∈ T^+(Q_p), at a K_p with an Iwahori decomposition (§1.3.4, p. 3). The monoid map t ↦ [K_p t K_p] comes from Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) SR.1–SR.2.
  - HigherHidaAndColemanTheory defines the ordinary part RΓ(S^tor_{K^pK_p}, ω^κ)^{ord} with these operators.

Layer 5. The single statement of Lan's Theorem 8.6 must also cover Proposition 5.6.3 (p. 58). The reference is K.-W. Lan, "Integral models of toroidal compactifications with projective cone decompositions", Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN 2017, no. 11, 3237–3280, Def. 8.5 and Thm. 8.6 (PILLONI-20's [50]). The case needed:
- modulo p, for ω^κ(−D) built from V_κ;
- on the Iwahori-level toroidal models defined by normalization and their maps to the minimal compactification (ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary, over the open models of ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII);
- in any genus (the paper uses g = 2);
- locally over an open of the minimal compactification.
HigherHidaAndColemanTheory checks Definition 8.5 for its Igusa sheaves.

Layer 6. Su's theorem for both complexes in every genus, with the exact statement taken from Su's paper. Also §1.3.7 as corrected. Together they extend CG20's Theorem 5.2 and PILLONI-20's H^0/H^1 statements to H^{ℓ(w)}.

Layer 7. §1.3.3, the genus-g form of CG20's Theorem 5.6(1).

Owned elsewhere:
- the dynamic and ordinary theory of §2, including Proposition 2.7.2 and Theorem 2.7.4 (HigherHidaAndColemanTheory);
- Theorem 2.7.1 and §2.9.5–Theorem 2.9.7 (AnalyticStacks AS.3);
- ^MW (ShimuraData D3, D5);
- C(κ) and Theorem 1.3.8 (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.4, AF.1). Theorem 1.3.8 is M. Harris, "Automorphic forms and the cohomology of vector bundles on Shimura varieties", in Automorphic forms, Shimura varieties, and L-functions, Vol. II (Ann Arbor, 1988), Perspect. Math. 11, Academic Press, 1990, 41–91, Thm. 3.4.

New imports:
- Six-functor formalisms and analytic stacks (AnalyticStacks) AS.0, AS.3: solid six functors, base change, D_X, supports, completions, the Cousin spectral sequence, and base change along Tor-independent squares (with AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension, already imported).
- Light condensed mathematics, solid abelian groups and analytic rings (SolidAnalyticRings) SA.3: Lemma 2.9.3.
- Shimura data, Hermitian domains, and adelic level structures (ShimuraData) D3: ^MW and the M-dominant cone.
- Parameter stacks, invariant theory and spectral coefficients (LanglandsParameterStacks) LP3: Weyl and dual Weyl modules over Z_p, here for M = GL_g × G_m. They are not taken from Reusable infrastructure for potential automorphy over CM fields (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure) PA.1, which lies downstream of PadicFamilies, IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration and AutomorphicBundles itself.
- Adic Spaces PartII (AdicSpacesPartII), stage AdicSpacesPartII:R3 (coherent sheaves and finite traces): the finite étale trace.

Already imported:
- AutomorphicBundles B4–B5;
- Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry (ShimuraCompactifications) C3–C4;
- Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry) A0-extension;
- Automorphic forms on reductive groups (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups) AF.1, AF.4;
- ShimuraData D5;
- Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) SR.1–SR.2;
- ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII;
- ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary.

Nothing comes from HigherHidaAndColemanTheory or from Algebraic modular forms, reduction and Serre weights, Part II: Siegel modular forms of genus two modulo p^n (SiegelModularFormsModPn).

Consumer: HigherHidaAndColemanTheory, in:
- §1.3.4;
- §2, including the T_n of §2.8 and the twists of Corollary 2.3.14;
- §4.3;
- §4.5 (Proposition 2.9.9 for t ∈ T^{++});
- §5.6.

Acceptance.
- For X, C flat over A, F coherent and A-flat, and M = A/I, T ⊗ 1 is the pushforward along C_{A/I} → C of the base change T′ to Spec A/I, after the base-change identifications of p₂^⋆ and p₁^!.
- For p₁, p₂ finite étale and T the identity of O_C, T^t is the identity for (C, X, p₂, p₁), via p₁^⋆ω_X = ω_C = p₂^⋆ω_X.
- ω_A = ω^{((1,0,…,0);−1)}; for g = 2, ω^κ and ν + ρ convert to CG20's ω(a,b) and Theorem 5.6(1).
- For g = 1 in weight one, Id and w_{0,M}·Id·w₀ both lie in C(κ) and give one π_∞, which contributes to H^0 and H^1 (E5).

routes.title: Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: integral models and reduction
routes.brief:
Joins ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII (parent ShimuraVarieties). PAPER-KISIN-MADAPUSIPERA-SHIN-22 proposed it as "Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: reduction and Honda–Tate theory". It was joined by PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25, PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26, PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-18, PAPER-KISIN-17, PAPER-VANHOFTEN-24, PAPER-GLEASON-LIM-XU-26, PAPER-FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24 and PAPER-PILLONI-20. Those briefs use several titles. This entry uses "Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: integral models and reduction", the title of the PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26, PAPER-FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24 and PAPER-PILLONI-20 briefs. The design job settles one title and merges the briefs. The roadmap starts where Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models (ShimuraVarieties) stops, after V8 and V8.general.

Source: G. Boxer and V. Pilloni, "Higher Hida theory for Siegel modular forms", Invent. Math. 244 (2026), 45–141, doi:10.1007/s00222-025-01393-2. "p. N" refers to the authors' version of 5 November 2025, and sourceIssues numbers are PAPER-BOXER-PILLONI-26's.

Conventions (pp. 33–34). G = GSp_{2g} is defined by the form on Z^{2g} with matrix (0 S; −S 0), where S is antidiagonal with entries 1. So ⟨e_i, e_j⟩ = 0 unless i + j = 2g + 1, and ⟨e_i, e_{2g+1−i}⟩ = 1 for 1 ≤ i ≤ g. P is the stabilizer of ⟨e_{g+1}, …, e_{2g}⟩, and B ⊆ P is the Borel subgroup that is upper triangular on the diagonal g × g blocks. A polarization's degree is the order of its kernel (p. 40; sourceIssues E65).

This paper adds two things: Siegel models at every level at p, normalized in products of de Jong's A_{g,d} with p | d allowed, and the genus-g Iwahori model of level p^n with its flag. PELModuli M4 normalizes only good-level models.

Layer 1: A_{g,d} (pp. 39–40).
- A_{g,d} → Spec Z is the stack of g-dimensional abelian schemes with a polarization of degree d² (de Jong, Math. Ann. 295 (1993)). Prove that it is a Deligne–Mumford stack of finite type over Z; it need not be smooth. PELModuli M2 does not apply when p | d. Over Z[1/N] with N ≥ 3, rigidify with a full level-N structure. Represent the rigidified problem with Hilbert schemes (R09.2) and the algebraic-stack results of R09.4, then glue over N = 3 and N = 4.
- Let δ = (δ_1, …, δ_g) be positive integers with δ_1 | ⋯ | δ_g and ∏δ_i = d. Set K_δ = M_δGL_{2g}(Ẑ)M_δ^{−1} ∩ G(A_f), where M_δ = diag(δ_1, …, δ_g, 1, …, 1). A_{g,δ} is the locus where ker λ is fppf-locally isomorphic to ∏ Z/δ_i × μ_{δ_i}. The printed "étale" does not work, and neither does the schematic closure of A_{g,δ,Q} (sourceIssues E63). Define A_{g,δ} as this substack of A_{g,d}. Only its generic fibre and its ordinary part are used, and the paper's "locally closed" is not claimed. Prove that A_{g,δ,Q} = S_{K_δ,Q} as stacks (K_δ contains −1) and that A_{g,d,Q} = ∐_δ S_{K_δ,Q}.
- Let 𝔄_{g,d} and 𝔄_{g,δ} be the p-adic formal completions, and 𝔄^ord_{g,d} and 𝔄^ord_{g,δ} their ordinary loci. On 𝔄^ord_{g,d}, the p-part of the type is read from the étale quotient of the p-primary part of ker λ, and the type is locally constant. The equality 𝔄^ord_{g,d} = ∐_δ 𝔄^ord_{g,δ} holds on underlying spaces; for g ≥ 2 it can fail as an equality of formal schemes, for example for g = 2 and d = p² (sourceIssues E63).
- Prove that A_{2,p} × Spec Z_p with prime-to-p level K^p is the paramodular Y_par,K of the Pilloni (2020) brief, so that it is built once.

Layer 2: normalization (p. 40).
- Fix K = K^pK_p. Choose positive integers d_1, …, d_r, types δ_i = (δ_{i,1}, …, δ_{i,g}) with ∏_j δ_{i,j} = d_i, and maps K ↪ K_{δ_i} given by conjugation by elements of G(A_f) followed by inclusion. Prove that these maps give a finite map S_{K^pK_p,Q} → ∏_{i=1}^r A_{g,d_i,Q}. S_{K^pK_p} is the normalization of ∏_{i=1}^r A_{g,d_i} × Spec Z_p in S_{K^pK_p,Q_p}. S_{K^pK_p,Z_p^cycl} is the normalization of ∏_{i=1}^r A_{g,d_i} × Spec Z_p^cycl in S_{K^pK_p,Q_p^cycl}.
- For K = K^pK_p ⊆ G(Ẑ) = K_{(1,…,1)} (so K_p ⊆ G(Z_p)), prove that the single factor A_{g,1}, with K ↪ G(Ẑ) the inclusion, recovers M4's model, the normalization of the good-level model S_{K^pG(Z_p)} in S_{K^pK_p,Q_p}.
- State Remark 3.4.21: S_{K^pK_p} will in general depend on the choice of the auxiliary spaces A_{g,d_i}. State Remark 3.4.22: the natural map S_{K^pK_p,Z_p^cycl} → S_{K^pK_p} ×_{Spec Z_p} Spec Z_p^cycl is in general not an isomorphism.

Layer 3: Iwahori level p^n (pp. 40–41).
- K_{p,n} is the subgroup of G(Z_p) of elements whose reduction modulo p^n lies in B(Z/p^nZ), with n ≥ 1 (printed n ≥ 0, sourceIssues E64). The generic fibre carries a self-dual chain A = A_g → A_{g+1} → ⋯ → A_{2g} → A_1 → ⋯ → A_g = A whose composite is multiplication by p^n. For 0 ≤ i ≤ g, Ker(A_g → A_{g+i}) is a totally isotropic subgroup of A[p^n], étale-locally isomorphic to (Z/p^nZ)^i.
- For 1 ≤ i ≤ g, A_{g+i} carries the polarization λ_{g+i} with π^∨ ∘ λ_{g+i} ∘ π = p^nλ, where π: A → A_{g+i}. Its degree is p^{2ng−2in} = d_i² (printed "= d_i", sourceIssues E65), so d_i = p^{n(g−i)}. Set d_0 = 1, so that the i = 0 factor is (A, λ). These points give S_{K^pK_{p,n},Q} → ∏_{i=0}^g A_{g,d_i}. S_{K^pK_{p,n}} is the normalization of ∏_{i=0}^g A_{g,d_i} × Spec Z_p in S_{K^pK_{p,n},Q_p}.
- Over S_{K^pK_{p,n}}, pull back A_{g+i} (0 ≤ i ≤ g) from the factor A_{g,d_i}. The members A_1, …, A_{g−1} come from no factor, so set A_j = A_{2g−j}^∨ for 1 ≤ j ≤ g−1. On the generic fibre this is A/H_{2g−j}^⊥, where H_{2g−j} = Ker(A → A_{2g−j}), because λ_{2g−j} ∘ π has kernel H_{2g−j}^⊥. Extend the isogenies of the chain from the generic fibre by normality (Faltings–Chai I, Prop. 2.7, from ShimuraCompactifications C4). The extension to semi-abelian schemes over the toroidal model S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} belongs to ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary.
- Let H_j = Ker(A → A_j), where the map is the composite along the chain. The flag is 0 ⊆ H_{g+1} ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ H_{2g} ⊆ H_1 ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ H_g = A[p^n]. Let Gr_j be H_j modulo its predecessor in the order g+1, …, 2g, 1, …, g, so that Gr_{g+1} = H_{g+1} and Gr_1 = H_1/H_{2g} (sourceIssues E66). Prove that over S_{K^pK_{p,n}} every H_j and every Gr_j is finite flat, and that Gr_j has order p^n. Also prove that H_{g+j}^⊥ = H_{g−j} for 1 ≤ j ≤ g−1, that H_{2g}^⊥ = H_{2g}, and that Gr_{2g−j+1} ≅ Gr_j^D. Along the boundary of S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} the kernels are only quasi-finite flat (sourceIssues E67).
- Remark 4.1.2 on the interior: prove that S_{K^pK_{p,1}} is the Iwahori lattice-chain moduli of the joined briefs. To do this, prove that this moduli space is finite over ∏_{i=0}^g A_{g,d_i} × Spec Z_p and has the same generic fibre. It is normal because its local-model diagram makes it flat over Z_p with reduced special fibre (Görtz, flatness of local models for the symplectic group), and its generic fibre is smooth. Take the local-model input from the symplectic-chain and reduced-special-fibre lane of GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII, and check that it covers p = 2. This is the genus-g case of the genus-two Iwahori chain of the Pilloni (2020) brief, which must be reused.

Imports (all upstream; none of them imports this route):
- Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models (ShimuraVarieties) V5, V8.
- Siegel and PEL moduli problems (PELModuli) M1–M5.
- Abelian Schemes And Arithmetic Moduli (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli) A2–A4.
- Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory) R07.1–R07.2.
- Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry) R09.2, R09.4, R09.6.
- Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry (ShimuraCompactifications) C4.
- Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations) SF.1.
- Shimura data, Hermitian domains, and adelic level structures (ShimuraData) D5.
- GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII (parent GeometricSatakeAndFusion, "Geometric Satake over the Fargues–Fontaine curve"), proposed by PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25 as "Geometric Satake over the Fargues–Fontaine curve, Part II: integral local models and residue-field curves".

Consumers:
- "Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry, Part II: integral boundary charts of Hodge type" (ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary) uses:
  - §3.4.23 (p. 40);
  - S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} and its chain of semi-abelian schemes (§4.1.1, p. 41);
  - the toroidal form of Remark 4.1.2, built on the interior identification made here;
  - the kernels Gr_j along the boundary, which are only quasi-finite flat (sourceIssues E67).
- "Igusa varieties, compactified period fibers and torsion concentration, Part II: ordinary Igusa formal schemes of Siegel varieties" (IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentrationPartIISiegelOrdinary) uses Lemmas 3.4.20 and 3.4.24.
- "Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes" (IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes) uses S_{K^pK_{p,n}} as the open part of the Iwahori-level toroidal models on which it builds M_dR and ω^κ.
- "Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology" (HigherHidaAndColemanTheory) uses §§4.1–4.3.

Acceptance tests:
- A_{1,p} ≅ A_{1,1}. The printed étale condition fails at the generic point of the ordinary locus of A_{1,p} ⊗ F_p.
- Let k be an algebraic closure of F_p and W = W(k). Take a k-point (A_0, pλ_0) with A_0 ordinary and λ_0 principal, and a basis e_1, e_2 of T_pA_0(k). The complete local ring of A_{2,p²} at this point is W[[x_11, x_22, x_12, x_21]]/((1+x_12)^p − (1+x_21)^p), where 1 + x_ij = q(e_i, λ_0e_j) are the Serre–Tate coordinates. Its reduction mod p is not reduced.
- For 1 ≤ i ≤ g, (A_{g+i}, λ_{g+i}) has type (1^i, (p^n)^{g−i}). H_{g+j}^⊥ = H_{g−j} for 1 ≤ j ≤ g−1, and H_{2g}^⊥ = H_{2g}.
- Take g = 1, p odd and K_p = ker(GL_2(Z_p) → GL_2(F_p)). Then S_{K^pK_p} lies over Z_p[ζ_p]. The p − 1 branches of Z_p[ζ_p] ⊗_{Z_p} Z_p^cycl meet in the special fibre, so S_{K^pK_p} × Z_p^cycl is not normal, and S_{K^pK_p,Z_p^cycl} → S_{K^pK_p} × Z_p^cycl is not an isomorphism (Remark 3.4.22).
routes.reason:
Sections 3.4.19–3.4.22 and 4.1.1 build integral Siegel models at levels other than hyperspecial level at p. They use four ingredients:
- de Jong's stacks A_{g,d}, with p allowed to divide d;
- their type loci and ordinary loci;
- normalizations of products of these stacks at any level, including over Z_p^cycl;
- the Iwahori model of level p^n, with its self-dual chain, flag and graded pieces.

This lies in the direction of "Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models" (ShimuraVarieties), which stops at canonical models (V8 and V8.general). The atlas does not plan it. "Siegel and PEL moduli problems" (PELModuli) M2 requires the polarization degree to be prime to p and allows no level at p. M4 only normalizes good-level models in higher-level generic fibres.

ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII already owns this direction. Its joined briefs normalize Hodge-type closures and build Siegel lattice-chain moduli. The Pilloni (2020) brief also builds the genus-two paramodular and Iwahori cases, which A_{2,p} and the n = 1 model must reuse. That brief also imports the symplectic local models from GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII, which the interior form of Remark 4.1.2 needs in every genus.

Each piece of mathematics has one owner. So this route joins that proposal with the same id and parent and adds only what is new. It uses the title of the PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26, PAPER-FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24 and PAPER-PILLONI-20 briefs, and the design job settles one title.

Three downstream proposals, named in the brief, own the rest:
- ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary owns the toroidal normalizations, including S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}}, its semi-abelian chain and the toroidal form of Remark 4.1.2.
- IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentrationPartIISiegelOrdinary owns the ordinary Igusa formal schemes.
- HigherHidaAndColemanTheory owns the cohomological use of these models.

Those proposals import this route, and this route imports none of them.

routes.title: Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry, Part II: integral boundary charts of Hodge type
routes.brief:
This route joins "Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry, Part II: integral boundary charts of Hodge type" (ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary). PAPER-FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24 proposed it, and PAPER-MAULIK-SHANKAR-TANG-22 and PAPER-PILLONI-20 joined it. The design job merges the four briefs. Source: Boxer–Pilloni, Invent. Math. 244 (2026), doi:10.1007/s00222-025-01393-2. Page numbers refer to the authors' version of 5 November 2025, and sourceIssues numbers are PAPER-BOXER-PILLONI-26's.

The additions start where the parent, "Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry" (ShimuraCompactifications), stops. Its C5 compactifies PEL moduli integrally at good level and normalizes that model at higher p-level. Pilloni's layers P1–P4 treat GSp4. The layers below go beyond them: they treat GSp_{2g} for every g, at any level K = K^pK_p with K^p neat.

§3.4.19 follows Lan (Forum Math. Sigma 4 (2016), e1) and Madapusi Pera (Ann. Sci. Éc. Norm. Supér. 52 (2019)). The joined briefs' Hodge-type models and Pilloni's X_par and X_Kli(p) are built by the same method. Building on PELModuli M4 and C5, the design job states the normalization theorem once for all four briefs. The theorem gives normality, properness and flatness for a normalization of the following kind: take a product of Siegel toroidal compactifications over a discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0, p), and a toroidal compactification of the generic fibre that is finite over that product; normalize the product in it. The models over Z_p below are instances of this theorem. Z_p^cycl is not a discrete valuation ring, so the variant over it is not an instance; G1 treats it separately.

Layer G1 (§3.4.23, p. 40). As printed: "We consider a finite map S^tor_{K^pK_p,Q} → ∏_{i=1}^r A^tor_{g,d_i,Q}. We let S^tor_{K^pK_p} → Spec Z_p be the normalization of ∏_{i=1}^r A^tor_{g,d_i} × Spec Z_p in S^tor_{K^pK_p,Q_p}. A similar variant holds over Z_p^cycl." Here d_i, δ_i and K ↪ K_{δ_i} are as in §3.4.19. Plan:
- A^tor_{g,d} over Z_p for every d, including p | d. This generalizes layer P2's X_par (g = 2, d = p). It is a proper algebraic stack whose generic fibre is ∐_δ S^tor_{K_δ,Q_p} for chosen cone decompositions.
